data.name: Kosha
data.long_meaning: In Hinduism, Kosha refers to the five layers of the human soul - Annamaya Kosha (physical body), Pranamaya Kosha (energy body), Manomaya Kosha (mental body), Vijnanamaya Kosha (intelligent body), and Anandamaya Kosha (blissful body). The name Kosha is derived from the Sanskrit word 'kosha' which means 'sheath' or 'container'.

data.cultural_impact: The term "Kosha" holds significant cultural importance in Indian philosophy and spirituality, particularly in the teachings of Hinduism. It represents the concept of the layered nature of the human being, which goes beyond the physical body. This belief is reflected in various Hindu texts and practices.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, Kosha embodies an essential understanding of the nature of the self and the universe. It reflects the belief in the interconnectedness of all things and the importance of treating the body, mind, and soul as a unified whole. The practice of recognizing and nurturing these different layers, through various practices such as meditation, yoga, and Ayurveda, is considered a path to self-realization and spiritual growth. The name "Kosha," therefore, carries a profound spiritual significance, embodying the essence of the spiritual journey in Hinduism.
